extracted.intended_audience: researchers and graduate students in geometric analysis working on Ricci flow and surgery (3‑manifolds)
extracted.subtask_description: Technical guidelines and a priori assumptions for constructing and continuing the Ricci flow with surgery on three‑manifolds: canonical neighborhood classification, surgery (δ‑cutoff) procedure, pinching and noncollapsing estimates, and related parameter choices ensuring finite surgeries and continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each point (x,t) with sufficiently large curvature has a neighborhood of one of two types: an ε-cap or an ε-neck; more precisely (Lemma 7.3.5) for any ε>0 there is C(ε) such that each Bt(x,2r) (for some 0<r<C(ε)R(x,t)^{-1/2}) falls into (a) B is an ε-cap, or (b) B is an ε-neck which, after scaling by R(x,t) and shifting time to zero, is ε-close (in the C^{[ε^{-1}]} topology) to the corresponding subset of the evolving standard cylinder S^2×R over a specified parabolic time interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ε‑neck alternative includes a precise parabolic neighborhood: after scaling with factor R(x,t) and shifting time to zero the parabolic neighborhood P := B_t(x,ε^{-1}R(x,t)^{-1/2})×[−min{R(x,t)^{-1},tR(x,t)},0] is ε-close to the evolving round cylinder with scalar curvature 1 at time zero. This assumption is used to identify necks for surgeries and to classify local geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong ε‑neck canonical neighborhoods in limits
rubrics_metrics.description: When taking pointed limits at high curvature points, the limit at each time has every point with a strong ε‑neck as its canonical neighborhood; in particular the limit is ε‑close to the standard round cylinder in appropriate parabolic regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce that the limit is κ‑noncollapsed and hence, by classification (Theorem 6.2.2), an evolving round cylinder S^2×R. The argument is repeated in time to extend the limit to an ancient interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ‑noncollapsed on all scales (definition and requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: A (surgically modified) solution is κ‑noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on scales less than ρ if whenever r<ρ and |Rm|≤r^{-2} holds on the parabolic neighborhood P(x0,t0,r,−r^2), then Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantitative noncollapsing condition is required at each stage to prevent degenerations; it is used repeatedly (via compactness theorems) to extract limits and to ensure finitely many surgeries in finite time. Proposition/Lemma references show how κ depends only on initial data in certain standard situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinching assumption (preserved under surgery)
rubrics_metrics.description: A curvature pinching inequality of the Perelman/Hamilton type must hold and be preserved under surgery. (See Lemma 7.3.4 / equation (7.3.9): after surgery the metric ˜g satisfies a pinching condition of the schematic form ˜R ≥ (−˜ν)[log(−˜ν)+log(1+T)]^3 whenever ˜ν<0, where ˜ν is the least eigenvalue of the curvature operator of ˜g.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lemma 7.3.4 asserts there are universal δ0,c0,P0 so that using the prescribed δ‑cutoff surgery with c=c0,P=P0 at small δ and suitable h one preserves the pinching inequality; the pinching inequality (7.3.9) is invoked to control curvature signs and to apply gradient/diameter estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: δ‑cutoff surgery procedure (definition and geometric constraints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform surgery by finding a δ‑neck N of radius h, cutting along the middle two‑sphere, and replacing the horn‑shaped end by a cap (B^3,˜g) constructed by gluing a fixed standard capped infinite cylinder C(c,P) according to formula (7.3.8) (using a bump function ϕ and the conformal factor e^{-2f}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choices c=c0 and P=P0 (universal constants from Lemma 7.3.4) and δ≤δ0 ensure the pinching condition is preserved. After surgery, metric balls of radius (1/2)h centered near the tip are, after scaling by h^{-2}, δ^{1/2}‑close (in C^{[δ^{-1/2}]}) to corresponding balls in the fixed standard capped infinite cylinder. The radius h must satisfy the parameter bounds required (see δ and h constraints) so that the surgery affects precisely the intended region.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard capped infinite cylinder and standard solution (existence and curvature estimates)
rubrics_metrics.description: A standard capped infinite cylinder is a rotationally symmetric metric on R^3 with nonnegative sectional curvature, positive scalar curvature, asymptotic to a semi‑infinite round cylinder of scalar curvature 1. The Ricci flow starting from such data (the standard solution) exists on a maximal time interval [0,T) with bounded curvature on compact subintervals and satisfies quantitative curvature estimates (Proposition 7.3.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 7.3.3 gives lower/upper curvature bounds depending only on the initial metric and yields κ‑noncollapsing on scales less than sqrt(T). Standard solutions serve as local models against which post‑surgery regions are compared.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local curvature control function ω (Claim 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists a positive function ω:[0,∞)→[0,∞) depending only on the initial metric and κ such that R(x,t) ≤ R(y,t)·ω(R(y,t)·d_t^2(x,y)) for all x,y and all t in the solution's time interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inequality bounds the ratio of scalar curvatures at nearby points in terms of scaled distance and is used in the rescaling/compactness arguments to obtain limits and to control geometry at infinity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery parameter bound ¯δ(t)
rubrics_metrics.description: A time‑dependent upper bound for admissible δ's for δ‑cutoff surgeries is fixed by ¯δ(t) = min{ (1)/(2 e^{2 log(1+t)}), δ0 } (equation (7.3.16)). One always assumes 0<δ<¯δ(t) for any δ‑cutoff surgery at time t and fixes c=c0,P=P0 accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This constraint ensures surgeries are performed at sufficiently small scales relative to time so that the pinching and canonical neighborhood assumptions remain valid after surgery. It ties the surgery scale to time to prevent pathological accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed surgical procedures at a surgery time T (summary)
rubrics_metrics.description: At a surgery time T the allowed operations are: (1) perform δ‑cutoff surgeries for all ε‑horns whose other ends are connected to Ω_ρ; (2) declare extinct every compact component with positive sectional curvature; (3) throw away all capped horns and double horns lying in Ω_ρ; (4) declare extinct all compact components lying in Ω_ρ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These four operations fully specify how the manifold is modified at surgery times: which ends are cut, which components are removed, and which are regarded as extinct. This list is used to ensure the surgically modified manifold still satisfies the a priori pinching and canonical neighborhood structures needed to continue the flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local standardness near surgery caps (Perelman Lemma 7.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given 0<ε≤1/100, 1<A<∞ and 0<θ<1, there exists ¯δ(A,θ,ε)>0 such that if surgeries use δ<¯δ and x0 is any fixed point on the gluing caps at surgery time T0 with h the cutoff radius around x0, then either (i) the solution is defined on the parabolic region P(x0,T0,Ah,T1−T0,T0+θh^2) and after scaling by h^{-2} is A^{-1}-close to the corresponding subset of the standard solution, or (ii) the same holds with T1 replaced by some surgery time t+∈(T0,T1) and BT0(x0,Ah) is cut off at t+ (every point in BT0(x0,Ah) terminates at t+).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides criteria that detect whether the neighborhood of a glued cap looks like the standard solution for a controlled time interval or else is removed at a subsequent surgery; it yields uniform control of post‑surgery geometry near the caps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau–Perelman length lower bound for curves near caps (Corollary 7.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: For any l<∞ one can find A=A(l)<∞ and θ=θ(l)∈(0,1) so that for the setup of Lemma 7.3.6 (with δ small), any smooth curve γ contained in BT0(x0,Ah), parametrized by t, with either T_γ = T1 < T or T_γ < T1 and γ(T_γ)∈∂BT0(x0,Ah), satisfies ∫_{T0}^{T_γ} (R(γ(t),t) + |γ̇(t)|^2) dt > l.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quantitative lower bound on the Perelman/L‑length of curves passing through surgery regions shows such curves incur arbitrarily large length if they stay in the gluing zone long enough; used to estimate and exclude low‑L curves that traverse surgery regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ε‑cap / ε‑neck classification for the standard solution (Lemma 7.3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the fixed standard solution on R^3 there exists, for each ε>0, a constant C(ε) so that any point (x,t) has an open neighborhood of size ≤C(ε)R(x,t)^{-1/2} which is either an ε‑cap or an ε‑neck (the neck described as the time slice of a parabolic neighborhood ε‑close after scaling to the evolving standard cylinder).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives the canonical neighborhood structure specific to the standard solution and is used as the model when checking post‑surgery neighborhoods for ε‑closeness to the standard cylinder or cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgery radii must depend only on δ and surgery time T (independence requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The radius h used for a δ‑cutoff surgery must depend only on δ and the surgical time T and must be independent of the particular surgical solution; otherwise one cannot guarantee cutting off enough volume at each surgery to obtain finitely many surgeries in each finite time interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This independence is emphasized as crucial: uniform control of surgery radii (as a function of δ and time only) ensures global volume/surgery count estimates and is required in induction/extension arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniform choice of r(t) and avoidance of accumulating surgery times (Proposition 7.4.1 requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ε>0 one can choose decreasing sequences 0<r_j<ε, κ_j>0, 0<δ_j<ε^2 and produce a time‑dependent δ(t) equal to δ_j on time intervals [(j−1)ε^2, jε^2) such that any surgically modified solution starting from normalized initial data and having only finite δ(t)‑cutoff surgeries (with δ(t) ≤ min{δ(t),¯δ(t)} at surgery times) satisfies on each time interval [(j−1)ε^2, jε^2) the κ_j‑noncollapsing on all scales <ε and the canonical neighborhood assumption (with accuracy ε) with radius r_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the scheme to choose surgery parameters uniformly across the inductive continuation of the flow so that surgeries do not accumulate and the canonical neighborhood assumption can be kept uniform (independent of the number of previous surgeries). The proposition describes how to partition time and pick parameter sequences to guarantee the required a priori properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: surgically modified solution κ‑noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on scales <ρ (formal check condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A surgically modified solution is κ‑noncollapsed at (x0,t0) on scales <ρ if for any r<ρ, whenever |Rm(x,t)|≤r^{-2} on P(x0,t0,r,−r^2) (i.e., on those (x,t) in Bt'(x0,r), t'∈[t0−r^2,t0] for which the solution is defined), we have Vol_{t0}(B_{t0}(x0,r)) ≥ κ r^3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explicit formulation (restated in Proposition 7.4.1) is the working criterion used to verify noncollapsing in surgically modified solutions; it is the condition to be checked in the inductive arguments and compactness applications.
